The test image shows dense white/pinkish fluffy mycelial growth on a stem/crown area with numerous small, round, yellowish-white sclerotia (mustard-seed sized). This pattern is highly characteristic of either Southern Blight (small round sclerotia) or Sclerotinia Timber Rot (larger, irregular sclerotia).

Let me view one reference from each of my top candidates.

The Sclerotinia Timber Rot reference (Bugwood_14) shows large, dark/black irregular sclerotia — very different from the test image.

**Analysis:**

The test image (Bugwood 1578614) shows:
- Dense white/pinkish fluffy mycelium at the stem crown/base
- Numerous small, round, yellowish-white sclerotia — mustard-seed sized (1-2mm), uniformly spherical

**Comparison:**
- **Southern Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii): produces exactly this — white cottony mycelium fanning from the stem base + small, round, numerous sclerotia that start white and turn tan/brown. This matches perfectly.
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**: sclerotia are much larger, elongated-irregular, and turn black when mature (as seen in the reference). Does NOT match.

The test image is a textbook close-up of Southern Blight.
